answer: The meadow multiplier is published, charged in cedar, and shale lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1366 identities would post 2366 proofs and burn roughly 79 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
